name: Vodafone Group Plc
moat_justification: Weak moat (4/10). Vodafone owns scarce spectrum and sunk network infrastructure in 15+ markets and is now the UK's largest mobile operator via VodafoneThree, with real scale in Germany (largest market), a majority stake in Vodacom with M-Pesa financial services in Africa, and a top-tier enterprise/IoT franchise. But connectivity is a commodity: switching costs are low, regulators cap returns and mandate wholesale access, MVNOs and price competition (Germany especially) grind ARPU, and ROCE has run below the cost of capital for years — the FY26 investor targets only promise ROCE above WACC by FY32. Scale buys survival and synergies, not pricing power.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 19 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.5%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency EUR converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion
USD_TRANSLATIONS_USED: the issuer files its own USD convenience translations alongside its reporting currency; the engine used the filed USD figures

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x10.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Vodafone Group Plc Form 20-F (filed 14 June 2024), cover page: American Depositary Shares 'each representing ten ordinary shares'; same ratio stated in the depositary (BNY) ADR records for CUSIP 92857W209) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.1x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 4.6x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier A (20.1%) vs bull-case tier S (32.5%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Post-restructuring telecom, moat 4/10 - engine 5.5 now subtracts Vodafone's filed intangible purchases and still prints Tier S by numbers (25.16% weighted IRR at $16.11, IV@15 $29.11, band A to S) because its OE is operating cash flow before lease payments and interest and its base years still carry Spain and Italy's operating cash flow; on Vodafone's own adjusted FCF (EUR 2.6B in FY26, EUR 2.6-2.9B guided for FY27) the ADS yields roughly 7% with low growth and net debt 4.57x normalized OE, so it does not clear 15% at $16.11 - final tier D by override, numbers tier S retained.
tier_override_reason: Engine 5.5 re-score (2026-10-19): the numbers tier is still S - weighted IRR 25.16% at $16.11, bear-case 20.07%, super-bear 13.51%, base OE $3.82/ADS - after the engine began subtracting Vodafone's filed intangible purchases (IFRS PurchaseOfIntangibleAssetsClassifiedAsInvestingActivities, EUR 2,799M / 2,641M / 2,375M in FY2023-25) on top of PP&E purchases. That closes the capex gap the 2026-10-14 override named, but the S still overstates the cash the business produces, for two reasons. (1) Perimeter: the engine's OCF is the 20-F's group total, which still carries the operating cash flow of Spain and Italy until their sale - EUR 3,464M / 3,296M / 1,657M in FY2023-25 (Form 20-F for FY2024 and FY2025, net cash flows from operating activities of discontinued operations, ifrs-full CashFlowsFromUsedInOperatingActivitiesDiscontinuedOperations) - while the capex it subtracts was restated to continuing operations; the median year, FY2024, is a full year before either sale. A continuing-operations base needs those filing figures, which this run's outputs do not print, so it is put to Andrew rather than pinned. (2) The OE is operating cash flow before lease payments and before interest, which Vodafone classifies as a financing cash flow (FY2025 Form 20-F); ruling 5 keeps both out of the engine. The figure the D rests on is Vodafone's own adjusted free cash flow (after capital additions, lease costs, interest and tax; before spectrum and restructuring): EUR 2.5B in FY25 and EUR 2.6B in FY26 (FY26 results, May 2026), guided EUR 2.6-2.9B for FY27 with the upper end expected (Q1 FY27 trading update, 27 July 2026), against the engine's FY2025 OE total of $9.262B. That comparison deducts interest as well as lease payments; beyond the Spain/Italy operating cash above, this run's outputs cannot split the gap between them. On the company's measure the ADS yields roughly 7% at the run's ADS-corrected $42.126B market cap, with net debt 4.57x normalized OE (HIGH_NET_DEBT), so a 15% IRR needs FCF growth Vodafone has never sustained - a D-tier return profile. Tier set to D; tier_by_numbers (S) retained in score.json.
moat_for: Scarce licensed spectrum + sunk network assets in 15+ markets
VodafoneThree: UK's largest mobile operator (~28m customers), GBP 1bn/yr synergy target by FY32
Germany scale: largest single market, cable/fibre footprint to ~75% of homes
Vodacom + M-Pesa: African growth and mobile-money franchise (Safaricom stake raised to 55%)
Vodafone Business: global enterprise, IoT platform (240m+ connections), digital services growing high-double-digit
moat_against: Commodity connectivity: low switching costs, MVNO and price competition, esp. Germany
Regulated returns: spectrum auctions, wholesale-access mandates, price interventions cap ROCE (below WACC for years)
Structural decline in legacy fixed/voice; OTT players capture the value layer above the network
Emerging-market/FX exposure: Turkiye hyperinflation accounting, EGP/ZAR volatility
Leverage constrains the investment race: net debt EUR 25.4B at FY26-end plus GBP 4.3B cash buyout of CK Hutchison's 49% of VodafoneThree
